architecture.mechanism: microstructured PDMS surfaces patterned with micro-cylinders inhibit barnacle larvae settlement via physical disruption and hydrophobic properties, while reducing near-wall turbulence and shear stress to lower hydrodynamic drag
architecture.intervention: Apply a thin, durable microstructured polymer coating (e.g., silicone-based) with cylindrical pillars (5–50 µm diameter, optimized for barnacle cyprid dimensions) to the vessel hull and propeller, designed to entrap a gas layer and disrupt larval adhesion while reducing boundary-layer turbulence
architecture.expected_effect: 50–70% reduction in biofouling accumulation (comparable to paper’s 59% antifouling rate) and 5–10% drag reduction (scaling from paper’s 7.2% at 100 rpm), restoring fuel efficiency and speed without biocides
architecture.falsification_test: Conduct a 6-month field trial on a 1,000 TEU sister vessel, comparing coated and uncoated sections via underwater inspections (fouling coverage) and fuel consumption logs at identical operating profiles; validate with CFD simulations of near-wall turbulence on microstructured vs. flat surfaces
